title: Pair Up Identical Values
statement:
You get an array nums with an even number of elements, 2n. Decide whether you can split it into n pairs so that the two numbers in every pair are equal. Every element must be used in exactly one pair.

A pair may use any two positions; they do not have to be next to each other. Return true or false.

examples.why: Pairs (4, 4), (4, 4) and (7, 7). The 4s are spread out, but positions do not matter.
5 appears three times, so one 5 is left without a partner.
No two equal values are adjacent, but (1, 1) and (2, 2) still work.

constraints: 2 ≤ nums.length ≤ 100 000, and the length is even
hints: Ignore positions. What has to be true about how often each value appears?
Every value must appear an even number of times. Count them.
You can even skip the counts: keep a set and toggle each value in or out. The answer is whether the set ends empty.

explain.intuition:
Since a pair can use any two positions, order does not matter at all. All that matters is how many copies of each value there are. A value can be fully paired exactly when it appears an even number of times.

So count with a hash map and check every count is even. A neat variant: keep a set of values that are "waiting for a partner". Each new value either finds its partner in the set (remove it) or starts waiting (add it). The array can be paired up exactly when nobody is left waiting at the end.
steps: Create an empty set of unmatched values.
For each number: if it is in the set, remove it; otherwise add it.
Return whether the set is empty.
pitfalls: Checking only neighbours, nums[i] === nums[i + 1], without sorting first. The third example breaks it.
Checking that the number of distinct values is at most half the length. In [5, 5, 5, 6] that holds, but the answer is false.

solutions.title: Sort and check neighbours
solutions.idea: After sorting, equal values sit together, so the pairs must be positions (0, 1), (2, 3), and so on.
solutions.space: O(1) extra (sorting a copy uses O(n))

solutions.title: Toggle a set
solutions.idea: A value waits in the set until its partner arrives. Everyone paired means the set ends empty.

followups: Return the actual pairs as index pairs, not just true or false.
Values are small (at most 500). Can you avoid the hash map?
